candidate.answerReason: The family has three girls and six boys, so Harriet has two sisters and six brothers, whose product is 12.

methods.label: Count the whole family
methods.explanation:
Harry is one of the boys, so the family has \(5+1=6\) boys and \(3\) girls. Harriet is one of those three girls, so her sisters are the other \(3-1=2\) girls. Thus \(S=2\).

All six boys are Harriet's brothers, so \(B=6\). Therefore
\[
SB=2\times6=12.
\]
The product is \(12\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses including or excluding one person from a group, followed by a basic multiplication fact.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is part-total reasoning when the family member doing the counting changes. The method includes Harry in the boys and excludes Harriet from her own sisters, then uses a multiplication fact for the requested product.

review.mathematicalCheck: Including Harry gives six boys, while there are three girls. Excluding Harriet from the girls gives \(S=2\), and all six boys are her brothers, so \(SB=2\times6=12\), choice C.
review.levelCheck: The explanation clearly handles who is included in each sibling count.
